The Police Inspector of R.T. Nagar Police Station submitted charge sheet against accused No.1 to 5 for the offences punishable under Section 498(A) of Indian Penal Code and Section 3, 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
2. Prosecution Case:

The marriage of CW1 namely Smt.Naziya and accused No.1 was solemnized on 05-12-2019 as per Muslim customs KABC030376532021 CC No.13171/2021 and rites, at that time,
Naziya vs Mohammed Nizamuddin on 4 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97162748/

2 accused persons demanded and received Rs.3 lakhs cash, gold ornaments, household articles and Rs.2 lakhs for construction of house from CW4 namely Smt. Nargis and CW5 namely Sri Mohammad Ismail as dowry.

After the marriage, CW1 was residing at House No.28, Bhavani Temple Road, 3rd Cross, R.T. Nagar, Muneshwar C Block, wherein, the accused No.1 to 5 with common intention picked up quarrel with CW1 and ill-treated her by not providing food and clothes to her and subjected her to mental and physical cruelty for reason of fetching additional dowry amount.

On 15-03- 2020, on the same issue, accused No.1 to 5 ill- treated CW1 for bringing Rs.15 lakhs as dowry from her parental house for business purpose, otherwise, accused No.1 would marry someone else and thrown her out of the house and thereby accused persons have committed alleged offences.
3. First Information Report:

On the basis of first information given by informant cum CW1, the Smt.Premakumari, CW10/WPSI of R.T. Nagar Police Station registered Crime No.264/2020 against the accused No.1 to 5 for the offences punishable under Section 498(A) IPC and Sec.3, 4 of D.P.Act,
prepared FIR and sent the same to the Court and drawn spot mahazar on 30-10-2020.
KABC030376532021 CC No.13171/2021 4.
Investigation:

Thereafter, CW11 Sri Ashwath Gowda,J., PI of R.T.Nagar PS recorded the statements of requisite witnesses, collected the documents and submitted the charge sheet against accused persons for the alleged offences.
5. On receipt of charge sheet, this Court had taken cognizance of offences alleged against the accused No.1 to 5.
6. The accused No.1 to 5 were enlarged on bail by the order dated 21-08-2025.

7. Copies of prosecution papers as required U/Sec.207 of Cr.P.C have been furnished to the accused No.1 to 5.
8.
Charge:

After hearing learned Sr.APP and counsel for accused, charge for the offences punishable U/Sec.498(A) of Indian Penal Code and Section 3, 4 of D.P. Act, has been framed, read over and explained to the accused No.1 to 5 in the language known to them, who, in turn, pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
. Prosecution Evidence:
The prosecution in order to establish its case cited 11 witnesses and examined 1 witness and exhibited 2 documents.

The learned Senior APP prayed for issuance of witness summons to other witnesses however his prayer was rejected on the ground that no purpose would be served as PW1 and the accused No.1 have agreed for dissolving their marriage amicably as per their Muslim customs and rites and hence the examination of CW2 to CW11 was dispensed with by the order dated 25-07-2025.

Statement of accused as per section 313 of CrPC: There are no incriminating evidences against the accused persons found from the evidence of prosecution thereby the recording of statement of accused as per Sec.313 of Cr.P.C. is dispensed with.
11. Heard the arguments.
Perused materials on the record.

12. The following point are arises for consideration is as follows:
1.

Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that after the marriage of CW1 namely Naziya with KABC030376532021 CC No.13171/2021 accused No.1, at that time, accused persons demanded and received Rs.3 lakhs cash,
gold ornaments, household articles and Rs.2 lakhs for construction of house from CW4 namely Smt. Nargis and CW5 namley Sri Mohammad Ismail as dowry thereby resulted in commission of an offence punishable under Sec.3 of Dowry Prohibition Act ?
2.

Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that after the marriage, CW1 was residing at House No.28, Bhavani Temple Road, 3rd Cross, R.T.
Nagar, Muneshwar C Block, wherein, the accused No.1 to 5 with common intention picked up quarrel with CW1 and did not provide food and clothes to her, subjected her to mental and physical cruelty for the reason of fetching additional dowry amount otherwise, accused No.1 would marry someone else KABC030376532021 CC No.13171/2021 and thrown CW1 out of the house and thereby resulted in commission of an offence punishable under Sec.498(A) of IPC?

3. Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that after the marriage accused No.1 to 5 subjected the CW1 to mental and physical cruelty for fetching additional dowry amount of Rs.15 lakhs from her parental house to do business thereby resulted in commission of an offence punishable under and Sec.4 of Dowry Prohibition Act?
4. What order?
13. The findings on the above points are as under:
Point No.1 to 3 : In the Negative Point No.4 : As per final order KABC030376532021 CC No.13171/2021 REASONS 14.
Point No.1 to 3: These points are taken up together for the purpose of common discussion in order to avoid repetition of facts as they form the same part of transaction.

In support of prosecution case as narrated in paragraph 2 and the point for consideration in paragraph 12 of this judgment, the prosecution has examined one witness, which is as follows:

4 i. CW1 by name Smt. Naziya, being informant examined as PW1 and identified her signatures on Ex.P1 (Complaint) and Ex.P2 (Spot Mahazar) as Ex.P1(a) and 2(a) and deposed that when she went to the police station for sorting out the minor differences of opinion amongst her and the accused No.1, the police obtained her signatures on the said documents and she pleaded ignorance about the contents of Ex.P1 and Ex.P2 and further deposed that she did not lodge any complaint against accused persons and no mahazar was conducted in her presence.
In this regard, the learned Senior APP cross examined this witness by treating her as hostile witness but no favorable answer has been elicited from her to support the prosecution case.

However PW1 admitted in her cross examination as under

On perusal of aforesaid recitation, it is clear that the disputes between the accused No.1 and CW1 (informant) have been settled and they obtained divorce as per their Muslim customs and rites.

16. This court places reliance in the case of B.S. JOSHI AND ORS. V. State of haryana and anr in KABC030376532021 CC No.13171/2021 the case of AIR 2003 SCW 1824, wherein it was held that,
"in a case where matrimonial disputes have been resolved between the parties then in that case offence under Section 498A of I.P.C. may be compounded between the parties for according to them an opportunity to settle in life afresh.

entities.text: B.S. JOSHI AND ORS. V. State of haryana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
and in the case of Ranjana Banerjee v. Bijay Bhushan Banerjee and Ors., 1996(2) East. Cri. C. 808 (Pat), wherein this lordship observed which runs thus:
"It appears that good sense have been prevailed amongst the spouses and when it became impossible for them to lead conjugal life any further and when the matrimonial home has been broken for all practical purposes, they have decided to withdraw all allegations and counter allegations against each other and get themselves separated on divorce by mutual consent.

entities.text: Ranjana Banerjee v. Bijay Bhushan Banerjee and Ors., 1996(2) East. Cri. C. 808 (Pat)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Although, Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code is not compoundable, but in the nature and circumstances of the case and the situation prevailing, accord is hereby granted to compromise the dispute between the parties and hence joint petition filed in both the cases are hereby allowed."

5 KABC030376532021 CC No.13171/2021

It further held that after examining the nature of the case and the circumstances, under which the offence has been committed, it would be proper to compound the offence and in my opinion, it would be also meet the ends of justice."
ADMITTEDLY, the disputes between the PW1 and accused No.1 have been resolved.
The criminal case under Section 498(A) of IPC and Section 3, 4 of D.P. Act are the off-shoot of the said matrimonial dispute.
The parties have come to their terms and in pursuance thereto the CW1/PW1 does not intend to proceed with this case and hence she has not supported the prosecution case.

17. In the case of the KRISHNA vs STATE OF KARNATAKA reported in Laws(Kar) 2014 4 464,
wherein it was held that "it would be unfair or contrary to the interest of justice to continue with the criminal proceeding or continuation of criminal proceeding would tantamount to abuse of process of law despite settlement and compromise between the victim and the wrongdoer and to secure the ends of justice, it is appropriate that criminal case is put to an end".
KABC030376532021 CC No.13171/2021 18.

entities.text: KRISHNA vs STATE OF KARNATAKA reported in Laws(Kar) 2014 4 464
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Under these circumstances and on account of the preposition laid down by the Hon'ble Apex and Hon'ble High Court, even if other witnesses examined by the prosecution, they did supported the prosecution, would not helpful to the prosecution.
Under these circumstances, this court feels it is a waste of precious time of the Court in examining other witnesses.
Moreover the evidence of other witnesses is only formal in nature.

Therefore, the prayer of learned Sr.APP is rejected and prosecution evidence is taken as closed and hence the ingredients for offences Under Section 498(A)
of IPC and Section 3, 4 of D.P. Act was not proved beyond reasonable doubt.
Accordingly, this court answer the point No.1 to 3 in the Negative.
19. Point No.4:-

In view of the above findings and reasons given on point No.1 to 3, this Court proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER Acting U/Sec.248(1) of the Cr.P.C.
(i) The accused No.1 to 5 are found not guilty and acquitted from the offences punishable under Sec.498(A) of Indian Penal KABC030376532021 CC No.13171/2021 Code and Section 3, 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
(ii) Accused are set at liberty.
(iii) In view of Section 437-A of Cr.P.C their bail bonds shall be in force for 6 (six)
months.
